note: Anchoring accuracy measured against real repository history. Regenerate deliberately, never to make a failing comparison pass. A rise in `wrong` or a fall in `correct` is a regression.
interpretation: The error profile is conservative by design: `false_stale` (declined to place a line that survived) exceeds `wrong` (placed a line at the incorrect location) at every drift depth. That ordering is the point of the two-threshold ladder, because a wrong placement points an agent at code that was never the subject of the note, while a false stale merely asks a human to look. Recall falls sharply with drift -- at 600 commits on a hot file only 12 of 55 surviving samples were placed -- which is expected, since `git blame` counts a line as surviving even when the block around it has become unrecognizable.
